about: Statements by others (the operator, institutions, studies) and how far they are tested. Status vocabulary: supported, published (one study, not replicated), pending (test planned), tension (contradicts another statement), unverifiable (as stated), contradicted.

claims.text: Costs of up to EUR 350,000 a year, partly financed by the Province of Trento.
claims.test: Provincial acts, civic access request, right of reply.

claims.text: 2010 cover of 76,400 m2; about 52% less ablation.
claims.test: Point measurement 31 Jul-29 Aug 2010, radiative terms only: about 59 vs 123 cm w.e. One station per surface. Covered area per year in the same article: 28,000 (2008), 37,300 (2009), 76,400 (2010), 57,800 m2 (2011).

claims.text: Up to 69% less melt; albedo about 50% higher than ice.
Used sheets reused as the installation The Invisible Mountain.
claims.test: What share of the material? Betti & Fleck 2021 (s9): 34 t laid a year, 17 t a year to the Bolzano incinerator as special waste, sheets used two summers. Waste records and operator still to ask.

claims.text: About 0.18 km2 of glacier covered in Switzerland; up to 350,000 m3 of ice saved a year.
The Presena glacier is a Site of Community Importance.
claims.test: Current Natura 2000 status; candidate site IT3120158.
Consistent with C02 and C03 (published field measurements).

claims.text: Covered areas absorb 36% of solar energy, uncovered areas 57%.
claims.who: Operator, attributed to University of Milan
claims.test: Found in AINEVA 74 (s2): albedo 0.64 fleece vs 0.43 unmodified glacier, 31 Jul-29 Aug 2010; absorbed 36% vs 57%. One site, one month.

claims.text: After six seasons the covers preserved 2.5 m of snow; uncovered ice dropped 11 m.
claims.test: LiDAR 2006-09 against 2014/2018. Context: AINEVA 74 observed a step of about 1.5-2 m after one summer (2010); Betti & Fleck report about 3 m of snow saved a season.

Sentinel-2 v3.6, preliminary, not validated (23 Nov 2026). Cover visible every summer 2016-2026. Visible area (lower-upper, m2): 2016 26,211-58,525 vs claim 50,000 (inside); 2017 26,612-51,823 vs 65,000; 2018 not usable (fresh snow); 2019 8,604-53,123 vs 100,000; 2020 5,302-87,638 vs 110,000; 2021 31,214-101,544 vs 110,000 (just above). Earlier runs (16 Nov) were lower; results changed as cloud, shadow, rock and snow errors were fixed. Other sources: AINEVA (s2) 76,400 m2 in 2010 and 57,800 m2 in 2011, above the operator's 40,000 m2 for 2014; Betti & Fleck (s9) 'more than 100,000 m2' in 2020, consistent with 34 t at 340 g/m2. Possible reasons for the gap with the satellite: fabric vs visible area, sheets under snow or in shadow, covers outside the zone.

claims.text: Partly financed by the Province, and carried out 'in total autonomy'.
claims.test: AINEVA 74 (s2, co-authored by the Province): the programme was approved by the Province, with an agreement between the Province and Carosello-Tonale spa (company created in 1987 when the municipality of Vermiglio bought the lifts, after Donati 2011). Tension with 'total autonomy' grows. Still needed: provincial acts, current ownership, ask the operator.

claims.text: 350,000 m2 of snow laid every winter; yearly loss of 600,000 m2 of ice mass.
claims.test: Units mix area and volume; ask the operator.

claims.text: Strips of 5 x 70 m, 500 g/m2, 4 mm thick, EUR 2/m2; more than 300 sheets.
claims.test: Weight in tension: Betti & Fleck 2021 (s9) give 340 g/m2; AINEVA names the fabric TOPTEX GLS 340 (Linz). Supplier and current product unconfirmed.

claims.text: A covered glacier will never disappear: it stays as a rectangular mass kept with snowmaking (2021 MUSE study).
Every year 34 tonnes of plastic cover the mountain; 17 tonnes go each year as special waste to the Bolzano incinerator.
claims.test: Waste records; ask operator and incinerator operator. Consistent with about 100,000 m2 at 340 g/m2.

claims.text: Covers reduce melt by up to 60%; about 3 m of snow saved each season.
claims.test: Compare with AINEVA (52%, step 1.5-2 m in 2010) and the LiDAR test (C09). No method given in the article.

claims.text: The Presena glacier has lost more than a third of its volume since 1993.
claims.test: Find the original source (provincial glacier monitoring?).

claims.text: The covers started in 2008 under a programme approved by the Province of Trento, with an agreement between the Province and Carosello-Tonale spa, and agreements with the Universities of Milan and Trento.
claims.who: AINEVA 74 (authors from Univ. Milan and the Province)
claims.test: Find the provincial act and the agreement text.
